name: Haiku growth at a reasonable price
strategy: AI infrastructure leaders with regulatory risk management: concentrated bets on MSFT and NVDA with durable competitive moats, balanced semiconductor exposure, elevated cash for volatility deployment
reassessment_note: OpenAI's safety pause on rogue agents signals emerging AI regulation risk; flat yield curve (10Y at 5.23%) now pressuring growth valuations despite strong AI earnings. Trimming extended semiconductor positions (AMD +18.61%, LRCX +16.93%) and exiting underperformers (CRM -9.13%, ADBE -7.78%) to lock in gains. Raising cash to 46% for tactical deployment and to absorb potential AI regulation headwinds. Maintaining concentrated core in MSFT and NVDA given exceptional earnings (NVDA Q2 +106% revenue, $108B guidance) and secular AI tailwinds.

positions.thesis: AI infrastructure dominance via OpenAI partnership, cloud computing leadership, embedded AI across Office/Azure stack. Best-in-class balance sheet and optionality. Current +3.86% gain locks in momentum.

Data center AI revenue +117% YoY (Q2 FY2027), $108B guidance for next quarter, first $100B quarter imminent. Dominant position in training and inference chips. Regulatory risk manageable given design moat and lack of direct consumer exposure to AI safety.

Network effects in digital payments, exposure to AI adoption in fintech, secular digitalization tailwinds. Stable business model resilient to rate environment. Current flat valuation allows for attractive risk-reward.
Defensive quality hedge in concentrated tech portfolio, consistent dividend and earnings growth, decoupled from AI regulation risk, resilient through rate cycles.
Quality holding with low correlation to AI and growth volatility, significant cash generation (4% yield on cash plus equity returns), portfolio hedge during regulation uncertainty.
Broadcom gains from AI infrastructure deployment (networking, broadband for data centers), less headline-dependent than foundries, well-positioned for AI chip ecosystem expansion.
Retain modest position for CPU/GPU AI acceleration exposure, but trimmed from 4% due to +18.61% run appearing extended. Stop-loss protects against competitive pressure from NVDA or foundry delays.
Semiconductor equipment plays manufacturing cycle upside as capacity expands, but +16.93% gain is extended relative to fundamentals. Trimmed position scales back leverage to equipment cycle.
Uncorrelated diversifier, small allocation preserves crypto upside (currently +30.68% since entry despite recent pullback), guards against currency debasement in 4% Fed funds rate environment.
